newsitem.title: MALI: Mali police use teargas to disperse protesters.
newsitem.headline: Mali police use teargas to disperse protesters.

text.p: Police in Mali's capital Bamako used teargas on Wednesday to break up protests by opposition militants to demand that elections be suspended and freshly organised after chaotic weekend polling, witnesses said.

Police patrolled the city in force after President Alpha Oumar Konare's government banned street protests when two opposition alliances urged their supporters to turn out in force to demand that Sunday's parliamentary poll be rerun and the government resign.

Witnesses said that police barred protesters from reaching the capital's Place de la Liberte square, focus of protests during the pro-democracy demonstrations that helped topple dictator Moussa Traore in 1991.
Groups of opposition militants, some numbering several dozen, walked around town chanting anti-government slogans. Police intervened when they tried to form larger groups, witnesses added.

The two alliance, which group 11 parties, urged their supporters to turn out in force on Wednesday to demonstrate their rejection of Sunday's parliamentary election during which severe organisational problems prevented many people voting.
Territorial Administration and Security Minister Lieutenant-Colonel Sada Samake banned all street protests in a statement issued on Tuesday.
